grand_strategy.reading: Peru is governed since 28 July 2026 by Keiko Fujimori, who won the runoff by 49,641 votes after Congress removed Boluarte (October 2025) and Jerí (February 2026): a right-wing president with the largest bloc in a new Senate but not a majority, a prime minister who is her vice president, and a cabinet built on investment and security. Peru is a minerals economy with two markets: China took 36.2% of 2025 exports, much of it through COSCO's Chancay, and the United States, the second market, now puts a 12.5% tariff on Peru, so Lima has to keep both open at once; its answer so far is to call the US a strategic partner, repair Mexico and Venezuela, and say nothing public on China. The strategy is held back less by enemies than by its own Congress and by borders it cannot close (Chile, Venezuelan migration), and the Chinese port is a political risk as well as a trade gain. Not verified for this card: Boluarte's and Jerí's removals and the Zhihua Yang meetings beyond the Wikipedia index, the Iran trade figures, the Section 232 copper tariff in force today, the Brazil, Spain, UK and APEC legs, illegal mining and the Shining Path remnants (no source read), and whether Peru's Congress ratified the Ilo protocol.

stances.note: Lima's side of the Chancay relation. The sources are mirrored from the CHN card (same URLs): the Chancay inauguration by video link on 14 Nov 2024 with Xi and Boluarte, a COSCO-owned terminal (60%, 30-year concession). Partner, not ally: no defence clause or alignment instrument was found. Warming on the volumes is our reading from the export figures (China 32% of 2025 exports, reported; not verified against the trade ministry). Friction sits under the posture: Congress removed President Jerí in February 2026 over undisclosed meetings with a Chinese businessman under scrutiny (Wikipedia pointer, tier 4). Update 2026-10-16: China took 36.2% of 2025 exports (Mincetur, via Infomercado; US$17.39bn in January-May 2026, +44.3%, Andina), Chancay handled 336,200 TEU in 2025 against a target above 350,000 and lost US$10.8m, and in early 2026 a Peruvian judge barred the regulator Ositran from supervising the port beyond its tariffs, drawing a US State Department warning and China's 'strong dissatisfaction'; Lima said the port must obey Peruvian rules. The new foreign minister Espa said nothing about China in the Reuters report of 31 Jul 2026 (silence, not a signal). No Peruvian government statement on China was fetched; the grade is our reading of the structure (C) on top of the mirrored B evidence. Bond none: no kinship or grievance found.

stances.note: Transaction, not alignment. The United States is named by Wikipedia as Peru's number one trade partner in total trade (tier 4 pointer), and the two cooperate on counter-narcotics and under the Rio Pact. Cooling: the 2025 push on copper tariffs (Andina reported a 50% copper rate in July 2025), and the Boluarte-era rift over US condemnation of rights abuses (Wikipedia pointer). Public opinion cools too: a CFR brief links the tariffs to a sour view of the US in Peru. Peru sends under 5% of its copper to the US, so the tariff is more narrative than volume (CFR, as seen in search results). The grade is our reading (C); no source names it. Bond none: no kinship or grievance found in the sources read. Update 2026-10-16: the tariff is now verified. On 24 Jul 2026 the US put an additional 12.5% tariff on Peru under Section 301 (forced-labour import bans; 10% or 12.5% for 60 economies), replacing the 10% Section 122 surcharge that expired that day, with 2,000+ products excluded (45% of the value of US imports from Peru); Mincetur says it will seek a review and has sent Congress a forced-labour bill. Against that, the Fujimori government (since 28 Jul) calls the US a "strategic partner" (Espa to Reuters, 31 Jul), expects a tariff review and is moving to join the US-backed Shield of the Americas against transnational crime; and in February 2026 the State Department warned that Peru could lose oversight of Chancay. Trend moved from cooling to stable: the trade friction and the political warming offset each other, our reading. US bought US$10.15bn of Peruvian goods in 2025 (Reuters via Hiru).

stances.note: Peru broke diplomatic relations on 1 Sep 2026 (consular ties kept), by a note delivered through Iran's embassy in Ecuador, which serves Peru. The foreign ministry gave four grounds: the deterioration of human rights as denounced by UN mechanisms, Iran's obstruction of IAEA inspectors, Iranian restrictions on shipping through the Strait of Hormuz since March, and Iran's 'incitement' of escalation in the Middle East, as the war restarted after new US attacks on Iran. stances_toward.note: Neutral and warming: a rupture healing. Peru severed relations on 3 Nov 2025 after Mexico granted asylum in its Lima embassy to former prime minister Betssy Chavez, accused of rebellion for Castillo's 2022 attempt to dissolve Congress; foreign minister De Zela called it an unfriendly act and the presidency accused Mexico of repeated interference; Sheinbaum called the break disproportionate (Andina, CP24). Keiko Fujimori, who took office in 2026, said in July she would restore relations, and on 7 Aug 2026 the two governments resumed them: Peru issued safe conduct for Chavez, under the 1954 Caracas Convention, and reserved the right to ask for her extradition (Reuters via Internazionale, Caretas). Mexico's Senate ratified Lydia Antonio de la Garza as ambassador to Peru on 13 Oct 2026 (Cronica); the Peruvian ambassador is unconfirmed (gap). The pair had no ambassadors since early 2023 per Reuters. Neutral and not rival: ties are back and no further act is read; bond grievance because the asylum wound is not closed (the extradition reservation) and echoes the Ecuador embassy case. Confidence B on the facts, the grade is our reading. Mirror of the PER card (written in parallel): it reads Mexico as reluctant_partner, warming, bond grievance; same trend and bond as here, and it adds that Peru's Congress had declared Sheinbaum persona non grata, that the 7 Aug restoration was a joint foreign-ministry statement citing ties of brotherhood, friendship and cooperation, and that Mexico also hosts Castillo's wife and children. Mexico's grade stays neutral because Mexico did not resist the restoration and shows no wish for distance, so reluctant_partner does not describe its side.

relations_from.summary: Bolivia's sea question on Peru's side: the Ilo protocol signed in October 2010 by Garcia and Morales gives Bolivia a duty-free maritime zone of 99 years at Peru's port of Ilo. Bolivia ratified it in February 2011; whether Peru's full Congress did is not verified. In January 2026 President Paz said the Pacific, through Chile or Peru, has to be Bolivia's gateway.
relations_from.note: From press reports of 2010 and from search summaries on the ratification; the treaty text and a Peruvian ratification instrument were not read. The 1929 Treaty of Lima is described in the same results as blocking Bolivia's access by both Chile and Peru, background not read in its text.

relations_from.summary: The Brasilia peace accords of October 1998 settled the Peru-Ecuador border after armed conflict; four guarantor states, the US among them, pledged US$40m for a border integration project and US$4m for demining. Peru's foreign ministry on 28 July 2026 called the relation a 'strategic priority' set by these accords and a Binational Cabinet continues to meet.
relations_from.note: The 1998 dates and the pledges come from the Wikipedia Foreign relations of Peru index (tier 4, cited as a pointer, not followed to its sources); the 2026 reaffirmation is from the Peruvian foreign ministry as reported by El Diario and Andina.

relations_from.summary: Santa Rosa island: after Peru's Law 32403 (July 2025) made it the district of Santa Rosa de Loreto, President Petro said on 7 August 2025 that Colombia 'does not recognize Peru's sovereignty' over it; Boluarte replied that 'there is nothing pending to discuss', the prime minister led a ministerial delegation and troops were deployed. Peru rests on the 1922 and 1929 treaties; Colombia says the island had not emerged when they were signed.
relations_from.note: Accounts differ on the Peruvian law (a June vote or a July law; the COL card gives Law 32403 of July 2025) and on the island's population (under 1,000 to about 3,000). No 2026 source was found, so the state of the dispute under the new governments in Lima and Bogota is not known.

relations_to.summary: Milei met Keiko Fujimori in Lima at the Torre Tagle on 28 July 2026, hours before her inauguration as president for 2026-2031, with Foreign Minister Quirno; the two agreed to strengthen economic, security and science cooperation. It was their first official contact; Peru's vice president-elect Luis Galarreta had visited the Casa Rosada beforehand. Paraguay's Pena, Ecuador's Noboa, Bolivia's Paz, Uruguay's Orsi and Chile's Kast also attended.

relations_to.summary: Colombia does not accept that Santa Rosa island, opposite Leticia in the Amazon, was assigned to Peru under the 1929 boundary arrangements and says it needs a bilateral assignment; Peru created the district of Santa Rosa de Loreto on the island by Law 32403 (July 2025) and says it lies on Chinería island, assigned to Peru in 1929. Petro went to Leticia on 7 Aug 2025 to restate the position. No source read says the dispute was settled or taken up by either new government (Fujimori took office in Peru in July 2026).

relations_to.summary: Peru severed diplomatic relations on 3 Nov 2025 after Mexico granted asylum in its Lima embassy to former prime minister Betssy Chavez, accused of rebellion over Castillo's 2022 attempt to dissolve Congress and facing up to 25 years; foreign minister De Zela called the asylum an unfriendly act and the presidency accused Mexico of repeated interference. Sheinbaum called the break disproportionate and said Mexico acted in line with international law; she said later that Mexico had not severed ties and Peru had started the break.

relations_to.summary: Peru and Mexico resumed diplomatic relations on 7 Aug 2026 under President Keiko Fujimori, who had said in July she would restore them; Peru granted safe conduct to Betssy Chavez to travel to Mexico under the 1954 Caracas Convention and reserved the right to request her extradition, and the joint statement gave no timeline. Mexico's Senate ratified Lydia Antonio de la Garza as ambassador to Peru on 13 Oct 2026; the two had no ambassadors since early 2023 (Reuters). Peru's ambassador to Mexico is unconfirmed.
